text:
eva: FYI saw a customer report where quota dashboards show spikes under the org project, but logs show calls were made with an impersonated project header.
frank: can you paste the trace? which headers are present?
eva: sample request we captured:
```
authorization: Bearer sa-impersonate-token
x-impersonated-project: project-42
x-origin-service-account: sa-prod-7
```
frank: and dashboard attribution shows `project-org-default`?
eva: yup — the quota-ingest pipeline appears to prefer the proxy-derived effective project over the `x-impersonated-project` header. customers get billed to org and confused.
gina: is impersonation a special case in the auth path? we treat `x-origin-project` differently from `x-impersonated-project` today.
harry: historically we ignored impersonated headers because they could be set by clients; the proxy was supposed to validate and swap to a canonical claim. seems some flows still leak the header before validation.
frank: leak how? order of middleware matters. if quota-ingest reads headers before the auth-exchange finishes, it will mis-attrib.
eva: exactly. we have a timing window where the auth proxy returns a 200 and the request hits routing before the exchange writes the resolved project header.
gina: short-term: add a small UI note on the quota dashboard showing "raw header project (if present)" vs "resolved project". can be behind a feature flag. low-risk.
harry: long-term we should make the proxy emit a signed `x-resolved-project` header and the quota-ingest must prefer that when present. signature prevents clients from forging.
frank: agree on signed header. also add telemetry: emit `auth.impersonation.resolved=true|false` and `auth.impersonation.source=header|claim|proxy` as span tags.
eva: for rollout: 1) dashboard UI flag to show both fields, 2) instrument telemetry at 10% sample to get baseline, 3) change ingestion to prefer signed `x-resolved-project` behind flag, 4) canary the signed-header flow for a subset of tenants, 5) flip if no regressions.
gina: add alert if number of requests where resolved!=raw_header > 1% for a customer over 1h — this will detect leaks/ordering issues quickly.
harry: owners: eva -> dashboard UI + support note, frank -> ingest change + signature verification, gina -> metrics & alert, harry -> proxy signed-header + canary config.
ci-bot: deploy scheduled: proxy/signed-header -> canary-2 (5 hosts) at 2026-03-25T02:00:00Z. See #release-war-room for logs. :rocket:
eva: support playbook update: include steps to check raw headers vs resolved project and how to request attribution fixes.
frank: also run a small smoke that replays known good impersonation flows and asserts quota attribution matches expected project. add it to canary checks.
gina: will add telemetry dashboards: time-series of `auth.impersonation.resolved` and a table of top tenants with mismatches.
harry: note: we must be careful with PII in logs — signed header payload should be minimal (project id + signature + timestamp) and we should redact any user ids.
eva: thanks team. once we have a 24h canary with <0.5% mismatches we can flip globally.
frank: tagging this as P0 for visibility with customers currently affected.
gina: cc @support-leads so they can proactively reach impacted accounts.
